svg.aria-label: The 3-2-1 backup rule mapped to a homelab. Three copies, on two different devices, with one off-site. Copy 1 is your live data on the NAS or server - the data you actually use, where RAID or a mirror lives, but redundancy is not a copy. Copy 2 is a local backup on a separate disk or box, on-site, for fast restores, built with restic, Borg or Kopia, Proxmox Backup Server, or ZFS replication. Copy 3 is off-site, in a cloud bucket such as Backblaze B2 or S3, or a box at another building, and it survives fire, theft and flood. A warning band states that RAID is redundancy not a backup, and a snapshot on the same pool dies with the pool, so neither counts as one of the three. The modern extension is 3-2-1-1-0: add one offline, air-gapped or immutable copy to defeat ransomware, and zero errors, meaning you verify and test-restore, monthly.
svg.text: The 3-2-1 backup rule, mapped to a homelab
Three copies, on two different devices, one of them off-site — and RAID is none of the three.
3 copies · 2 different devices · 1 off-site
Your live data counts as copy 1. So you still need two more — a local backup, and an off-site copy.
COPY 1 — THE DATA ITSELF
Live data on your NAS
The data you actually use, day to day,
on your server, NAS or desktop.
RAID / a mirror lives here —
but redundancy is not a copy
A deleted or encrypted file is gone
from every disk in the array at once.
COPY 2 — LOCAL BACKUP
A separate disk or box
On-site, on different hardware.
This is the copy you restore from
fastest when something breaks.
restic / Borg / Kopia · PBS
or ZFS snapshot + replication
“2 media” today just means two
separate devices — not tape vs disk.
COPY 3 — OFF-SITE (the one people skip)
Somewhere else entirely
A cloud bucket — Backblaze B2, S3 —
or a box at a friend’s house.
Survives fire, theft, flood
restic → B2 ≈ $1.40/mo for 200 GB
“More than a few miles away,” so one
local disaster can’t take all three.
Paying a host is not the same as
them running 3-2-1 for you — check the SLA.
RAID is redundancy, not a backup — and a snapshot on the same pool dies with the pool
Both survive a single dead drive. Neither survives deletion, ransomware, a bad update, theft or fire. Neither is one of the three.
The modern extension — 3-2-1-1-0
+1 one copy offline, air-gapped or immutable (object lock) — the copy ransomware can’t reach or rewrite.
0 zero errors — a backup isn’t a backup until you’ve verified it and actually run a restore. Test monthly.
Rule per Backblaze, Veeam & Nakivo; homelab mapping from restic, Proxmox Backup Server, OpenZFS & rclone docs; RAID-isn’t-backup from r/selfhosted & r/DataHoarder. TechFuelHQ.
